summary:
After The Signal is an interactive digital museum exploring the legacy of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the project presents four historical mission artifacts: the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), the Viking 1 Lander, and Mars Pathfinder.

Through dedicated artifact pages, historical records, NASA archival photographs, and an interactive mission timeline, visitors can explore what these technologies were designed to do and what they left behind. The museum also presents selected Apollo 15 Heat Flow Experiment observations from NASA's Planetary Data System through scientific data visualizations.

Our goal is to make space exploration history more accessible, connect scientific records with human storytelling, and preserve the stories of equipment that remained after the missions ended.
details:
Project Overview

After The Signal is an interactive digital museum created to explore the legacy of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. The project addresses the challenge of preserving and communicating the stories of space exploration hardware that remained on extraterrestrial surfaces after their missions ended.

The museum presents four historical mission artifacts: the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), the Viking 1 Lander, and Mars Pathfinder with its Sojourner rover.

How the Project Works

Visitors explore the museum through dedicated artifact pages, a mission timeline, and curated archival sections. Each artifact page provides historical context, explains the equipment's purpose and contribution to its mission, and connects visitors with original NASA photographs, mission documentation, technical records, and scientific resources.

The ALSEP section includes scientific data visualizations based on selected Apollo 15 Heat Flow Experiment records from NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS). These visualizations help visitors engage with historical scientific measurements rather than simply reading descriptions of the mission.

The interactive timeline connects important mission events and allows visitors to explore the historical development of these artifacts.

Project Demonstration Video

The project demonstration video provides a short visual walkthrough of After The Signal. It introduces the digital museum and showcases its main sections, including the four historical artifacts, their dedicated pages, the interactive mission timeline, and the scientific data visualizations based on Apollo 15 Heat Flow Experiment records.

The video allows viewers to see how the museum presents historical documentation, archival imagery, and scientific information in an accessible and connected format.

AI-generated music was used as background audio in the project demonstration video. The music was generated using Claude.

Benefits and Intended Impact

After The Signal transforms scattered historical and scientific resources into an accessible educational experience. It helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts understand not only what these artifacts were, but also why they mattered and what scientific and historical legacy they left behind.

The project aims to encourage curiosity about planetary exploration, improve access to space history, and demonstrate the continuing value of preserving scientific records and mission hardware.

Tools and Development

The project was developed as a public website using Wix. HTML and CSS were used to create and customize interactive sections, layouts, archival cards, and data visualizations. JavaScript was used where needed for interactive website elements.

NASA archival materials, mission documentation, historical photographs, and scientific datasets were consulted to support the museum's content. AI tools assisted with selected coding tasks and editing descriptive text; the research, project direction, content selection, and final decisions were handled by the team.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The project's central idea is to tell the stories of space exploration through the equipment that remained after the missions. Instead of presenting isolated facts in a conventional list, After The Signal combines historical storytelling, archival research, scientific data, and interactive navigation in one digital museum.

The team considered historical accuracy, source attribution, accessibility, clarity of information, and usability across desktop and mobile devices throughout development.

Sources and Attribution

Additional mission-specific references, scientific records, historical documents, and image credits are provided in the Primary Sources and Scientific Records sections of the corresponding artifact pages on our project website.
